newsitem.title: FRANCE: Channel Tunnel experts' report not complete.
newsitem.headline: Channel Tunnel experts' report not complete.

text.p: A French state prosecutor said on Monday that experts studying the cause of a fire that seriously damaged a section of the Channel Tunnel last November had not yet reached a conclusion.

"I do not yet have the conclusions of their appraisal in my possession," said Gerald Lesigne, the prosecutor in Boulogne-Sur-Mer charged with handling the probe. "As soon as I have them, I will hold a press conference."
A fire broke out on a lorry on a Shuttle freight wagon operated by Eurotunnel SA/Plc on November 18, causing severe damage and disrupting passenger and freight services in the first half of the year.
Lesigne refused to comment on British newspaper reports that the fire was the result of "a criminal act".
On Sunday Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle said the judicial probe into the fire had cleared the company of responsibility for the blaze.
"Neither Eurotunnel nor the lorry company is responsible," Patrick Ponsolle told Europe 1 radio.
Ponsolle said that a judicial inquiry into the causes of the fire would be made public in the near future but he refused to be drawn on whether it was an act of arson.
"One is never immune from criminal acts," he said.
But the inquiry had already shown Eurotunnel's installations and systems were not to blame for the fire, he said.

Eurotunnel shareholders are due to vote on Thursday on a plan to restructure its 70 billion francs ($11.9 billion) of junior-ranked bank debt, needed to ensure its financial survival. ($ = 5.891 French Francs)
